chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: It is not permissible for the one praying to pray while in a state of minor ablution (wudu) unless he performs another ablution.
And it is not permissible for him to pray in a state of major impurity (janabah) unless he performs another ritual bath (ghusl).
And it is not permissible for him to pray in a state of minor impurity (hadath) unless he performs another ablution.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying while in a state of minor or major impurity?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that the validity of Salah is contingent upon the removal of both minor impurity (hadath) and major impurity (janabah), emphasizing that the specific purification ritual (wudu or ghusl) must be performed anew if the state of impurity persists. This hadith underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that ritual purity is not merely a physical state but a spiritual prerequisite for standing before Allah, linking the physical act of washing to the metaphysical requirement of cleanliness in worship. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the interplay between fiqh (jurisprudence) and hadith in establishing the conditions for valid prayer.
